task: lowcomm-training milestone 6s: does the size-2 compression knee move with H? (H = 16, keep 1/8 and 1/32, plus keep 1/4 seeds 2-3)

doc_friction.issue: Warns that pyenv.py torch can take 18-35 min; this run it installed the CPU wheel on /usr/bin/python3.13 in under a minute. Fine as a worst case, but the expected case is now fast.
After pyenv's pip install, every python3 call prints a '_distutils_hack' traceback on stderr (harmless); it polluted the run log, which had to be filtered before commit.
110-char title limit is only learnt by running the checker; the post template in the last lowcomm post does not mention it.

notes: Hypotheses H6s-i..iii and analysis script registered and pushed (commit 1) before 10 training runs (~55 min, 4 cores). All three refuted: at H = 16 the rand-k excess is proportional to omega (0.0031/omega, chi2 2.5 on 3 dof; +0.003, +0.022, +0.045, +0.098 at omega 3, 7, 15, 31), no knee (w0 0-1.5 vs 6.5-9.0 at H = 64). Curves cross near omega 15. Checks run locally: project tests 12 passed; research/_homepage/build.py ok; research_live_links 0 updates; check_md_links ok; post frontmatter/links/similarity ok. Version-offset check: new omega-3 seeds on torch 2.15 match older seeds.

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
